newsitem.title: UK: Oman plans to develop bond market -minister.
newsitem.headline: Oman plans to develop bond market -minister.

text.p: Omani banks and companies may start issuing bonds in the domestic market within the next 18 months, Minister of State for Development Affairs Mohamed Musa al-Yousef said on Friday.
Yousef, who was in London to meet investors ahead of Oman's first international bond issue, expected in the first week of March, said Omani companies were being encouraged to issue bonds.

"The government has (in the past) provided medium and long-term loans to the private sector. Now these loans will be partly subsidised by the government, but they will be provided by commercial banks," he said.
"It will be a gradual evolution, but within the next 18 months we will see some bond issues. Banks may issue bonds, and the private sector itself may borrow directly from the market."
The only domestic debt instruments now available in Oman are government development bonds, he said.
Omani officials are traveling around the world in an effort to sell investors the country's first international bond issue.
Bankers said the five-year deal could be for at least $150 million. Yousef declined to comment on terms of the deal.
